definition: existing in large numbers or happening often; usual rather than rare

collocations.example: Working from home has become common practice at our firm.
Smith is a very common name in Britain.

definition: a group of people who live in the same area or share interests

collocations.example: The new library serves the whole local community well.
They held the charity meeting at the community center.

definition: to look at two or more things to see how they are alike or different

collocations.example: Always compare prices before you buy a new laptop.
We compared our results with last year's figures.

definition: a situation in which people or companies try to be more successful than others

collocations.example: Our company faces fierce competition from overseas rivals.
Market competition usually keeps prices low for consumers.

definition: to say that you are unhappy or dissatisfied with something

collocations.example: Several customers complained about the slow delivery service.
She complained to the manager about the noise.

definition: to make something more difficult to understand or deal with

collocations.example: Adding more rules will only complicate matters further.
The new software complicated the task for everyone.

definition: to give all your attention to one thing

collocations.example: I can't concentrate on my work with this noise.
You need to concentrate hard during the final exam.

definition: the state that someone or something is in

collocations.example: The used car is still in very good condition.
They keep the machines in excellent working condition.

definition: to mistake one person or thing for another

collocations.example: People often confuse me with my twin brother.
The two brands are easily confused by shoppers.

definition: to join two or more things together

collocations.example: Connect the printer to your computer with this cable.
An engineer came to connect up the new router.

definition: noticing or aware of something

collocations.example: She is very conscious of the risks involved.
Our factory staff are highly safety conscious at work.

definition: happening all the time or again and again

collocations.example: He works under constant pressure to meet tight deadlines.
This entrance is in constant use all day long.

definition: the act of communicating with someone

collocations.example: I stay in contact with my old colleagues.
We tried to make contact with the supplier.

definition: to have something inside

collocations.example: This drink does not contain any alcohol at all.
The report contains important information about the budget.

definition: a written legal agreement between two people or companies

collocations.example: We signed a two-year contract with the supplier.
She read her employment contract before starting work.

definition: to give money, help, or ideas to something

collocations.example: Everyone was asked to contribute to the farewell gift.
Local businesses contribute money to the school fund.

definition: to make someone believe that something is true

collocations.example: She convinced her boss of the plan's real value.
The committee was hard to convince at first.

definition: a police officer (an informal word)

collocations.example: A traffic cop pulled us over for speeding.
An undercover cop arrested the two thieves quietly.

definition: to deal successfully with a difficult situation

collocations.example: Fit people can cope with stress more easily.
She had to cope alone after the big move.

definition: something made to look exactly like another thing

collocations.example: Please send me a copy of the report.
I printed a hard copy for the meeting.

definition: right or accurate; without mistakes

collocations.example: Only one of the four answers is correct.
I think you made the correct decision here.

definition: a small house, usually in the countryside

collocations.example: They rented a small country cottage for the summer.
The thatched cottage looked charming in the sunlight.

definition: a soft white material used to make cloth

collocations.example: These shirts are made of soft pure cotton.
The dress is made from light cotton fabric.

definition: a condition that makes you push air noisily from your throat

collocations.example: She has had a dry cough all week.
He stayed home with a bad cough today.

definition: a group of people elected to manage a town or organization

collocations.example: The city council approved the new park plan.
She was recently elected to the local council.

definition: a flat surface where you are served in a shop

collocations.example: She was serving customers from behind the counter.
Please collect your order at the service counter.

definition: land outside towns and cities, with fields and farms

collocations.example: They bought a house in the quiet countryside.
We drove through miles of green rolling countryside.

definition: an area of a country with its own local government

collocations.example: Every autumn we visit the local county fair.
The county council manages the roads and schools.

definition: a child of your aunt or uncle

collocations.example: My first cousin lives just down the street.
She is a distant cousin of mine.

definition: a large female farm animal kept for milk

collocations.example: The farmer milks each dairy cow every morning.
A large herd of cows crossed the quiet road.

definition: a thin line or gap where something is broken

collocations.example: Water leaked from a crack in the pipe.
There is a small crack in the window.

definition: an accident in which a vehicle hits something

collocations.example: He survived the car crash without any injuries.
The plane crash claimed over a hundred lives.

definition: to move slowly with your body close to the ground

collocations.example: Our baby has just started to crawl.
He had to crawl along the narrow tunnel.

definition: the thick fatty part of milk

collocations.example: She served the apple pie with fresh cream.
He added whipped cream to his hot coffee.

definition: to make something new exist

collocations.example: The new factory will create hundreds of jobs.
Successful businesses create wealth for the whole country.

definition: a living thing such as an animal

collocations.example: Every living creature needs water to survive.
The panda is a shy, gentle creature.

definition: a way of buying things and paying for them later

collocations.example: Does the hotel accept credit cards for payment?
They bought the new furniture on credit.

definition: to move slowly and quietly to avoid being noticed

collocations.example: The cat tried to creep up on the bird.
We crept along the dark hallway without a sound.

definition: relating to crime or illegal acts

collocations.example: She is studying criminal law at university.
He has no previous criminal record at all.

definition: pleasantly hard, dry, and easy to break

collocations.example: Bake the potatoes until they are nice and crisp.
He likes crisp bacon with his morning eggs.

definition: a large number of people gathered together

collocations.example: A large crowd gathered outside the stadium gates.
The excited crowd cheered for the home team.

definition: a circular gold object worn on the head by a king or queen

collocations.example: Only the king may wear the gold crown.
The queen's gold crown was set with jewels.

definition: causing pain or suffering to others on purpose; unkind

collocations.example: He was cruel to the frightened young animals.
The prisoners suffered cruel treatment for many years.

definition: the customs, beliefs, and way of life of a group

collocations.example: Travel helps you understand a different local culture.
The festival celebrates the region's traditional culture.

definition: a medicine or treatment that makes an illness go away

collocations.example: Scientists are searching for a cure for cancer.
Doctors hope to find a cure very soon.

definition: wanting to know or learn about something

collocations.example: The children were curious about the new teacher.
Young kids are naturally curious about everything around them.

definition: to form into a curved or rounded shape

collocations.example: The cat likes to curl up by the fire.
The smoke curled around the empty, silent room.

definition: happening or existing now

collocations.example: The current situation at work is very stressful.
She is quite unhappy in her current job.

definition: a person who buys goods or services from a shop or business

collocations.example: She is a regular customer at our café.
A satisfied customer often returns to buy more.

definition: physical harm that makes something less useful or valuable

collocations.example: The storm caused serious damage to the roof.
Heavy trucks can cause damage to old bridges.

definition: to be brave enough to do something

collocations.example: She didn't dare to tell him the truth.
He wouldn't dare argue with the boss.

definition: the time of day when light first appears

collocations.example: The soldiers began their long march at dawn.
We left the house before dawn to travel.

definition: money that you owe to someone

collocations.example: The company is deeply in debt this year.
She worked hard to pay off her debt.

definition: the twelfth and last month of the year

collocations.example: Our busiest sales period is in December.
The whole project should finish by late December.

definition: good enough; of a satisfactory quality

collocations.example: She finally found a decent job in the city.
The workers want decent pay for their effort.

definition: a choice that you make after thinking carefully

collocations.example: We need to make a decision by Friday.
The board announced its final decision today.

definition: a floor or level of a ship or boat

collocations.example: All the sailors were called up on deck.
The passengers relaxed on the sunny upper deck.

definition: to make something look more attractive by adding things

collocations.example: They decorated the hall with balloons and flowers.
She decorated the cake with fresh strawberries and cream.

definition: the act of protecting someone or something from attack

collocations.example: He spoke in defense of his young colleague.
The country spends billions on national defense.

definition: a feeling of great pleasure and happiness

collocations.example: The children screamed with delight at the clown.
She takes great delight in her flower garden.

definition: to take goods to a person or place

collocations.example: They promised to deliver the goods by Friday.
The courier always delivers the parcels on time.

definition: the desire of customers to buy a product or service

collocations.example: There is strong demand for electric cars now.
Skilled engineers are always in demand.

definition: to say that something is not true

collocations.example: He continued to deny everything the police asked.
She flatly denied taking the missing money.

definition: one part of a large organization or company

collocations.example: He works in the sales department downtown.
She was recently promoted to head of department.

definition: to make someone feel sad and without hope

collocations.example: The constant rain began to depress the whole family.
Sad news like this can depress the spirits.

definition: to say what someone or something is like

collocations.example: Witnesses described the thief as tall and thin.
Please describe the problem in detail for us.

definition: a large dry area of land with little water

collocations.example: Few plants grow in the dry sandy desert.
They drove for hours across the hot desert.

definition: to have earned something because of your actions

collocations.example: The players deserve a reward for their effort.
After months of work, she richly deserves this promotion.

definition: the way something is planned and made

collocations.example: The chair has a simple but elegant design.
Our team handles all the product design work.

definition: a strong feeling of wanting something

collocations.example: His desire for revenge drove all his actions.
She has a strong desire to succeed.

definition: a table where you sit to write or work

collocations.example: Please leave the key at the front desk.
She was sitting quietly at her desk.

definition: feeling that you have no hope and will do anything

collocations.example: The stranded hikers were desperate for fresh water.
He found himself in a desperate situation.

definition: to damage something so badly it cannot be used

collocations.example: The fire completely destroyed the old wooden building.
They tried to destroy the evidence of the crime.

definition: a small individual fact or piece of information

collocations.example: The guide explained the plan in great detail.
She remembered every detail of the long meeting.

definition: to discover or notice something that is hard to see

collocations.example: The new test can detect the disease early.
Sensors detect any change in the room temperature.

definition: to find out or decide something exactly

collocations.example: Engineers worked hard to determine the cause of failure.
Rescuers used radio signals to determine the hikers' exact location.

definition: to grow or make something grow bigger or better

collocations.example: The small shop developed into a large chain.
Training helps workers develop new skills quickly.

definition: the food that a person usually eats

collocations.example: A balanced diet keeps your body strong and healthy.
A healthy diet includes plenty of fresh fruit and vegetables.

definition: to eat dinner, especially a formal meal

collocations.example: We like to dine out every Friday evening.
The whole family dined together on Sunday afternoon.

definition: going straight to a place without stopping or turning

collocations.example: We booked a direct flight to Tokyo.
The driver took the most direct route home.

definition: controlled and guided the making of a film or show

collocations.example: She directed several popular films last year.
The movie was directed by a famous director.

definition: the way that someone or something moves or faces

collocations.example: The wind suddenly changed direction during the storm.
She walked quickly in the direction of home.

definition: to stop being seen; to go out of sight

collocations.example: The bus disappeared into the thick morning fog.
The important documents seemed to suddenly disappear overnight.

definition: to make someone sad by not being as good as hoped

collocations.example: The new movie did not disappoint its fans.
She worked hard so as not to disappoint her parents.

definition: training that makes people obey rules and control themselves

collocations.example: The school is known for its strict discipline.
Good teachers maintain discipline in the classroom.

definition: to talk about something with other people

collocations.example: I will discuss the plan with my manager.
They met to discuss the matter in private.

definition: an illness that affects people, animals, or plants

collocations.example: Smoking greatly increases the risk of heart disease.
Dirty water can spread disease very quickly.

definition: a strong feeling of dislike or disapproval

collocations.example: He threw down the report in disgust.
Many viewers felt disgust at the cruel scenes.

definition: food prepared in a particular way as part of a meal

collocations.example: The chef recommended the fish as a main dish.
We ordered a green salad as a side dish.

definition: the amount of space between two places or things

collocations.example: They traveled a long distance to reach us.
The distance between the two towns is small.

definition: an area of a town or country

collocations.example: The company's main office is in the business district.
They live in a quiet residential district.

definition: to interrupt someone or stop them concentrating

collocations.example: Please do not disturb the staff during meetings.
I didn't want to disturb you while working.

definition: to jump into water with your head and arms first

collocations.example: She loves to dive into the cool pool.
The boys dived off the high rocks.

definition: to separate something into parts or groups

collocations.example: The teacher divided the class into four groups.
We agreed to divide up the work fairly.

definition: the legal ending of a marriage

collocations.example: The divorce rate has risen in recent years.
She decided to file for divorce last spring.

definition: a child's toy shaped like a small person

collocations.example: The little girl carried her favorite rag doll.
She bought a baby doll for her niece.

definition: the unit of money used in the US and some other countries

collocations.example: The US dollar rose against the euro today.
He handed me a crisp ten dollar bill.

definition: a group of twelve things

collocations.example: She bought a dozen eggs at the market.
We ordered half a dozen chairs for the office.

definition: to pull something heavy along the ground

collocations.example: He had to drag the heavy box along the floor.
They dragged the small boat across the wet sand.

definition: an imaginary animal that can breathe fire

collocations.example: The story tells of a fierce fire-breathing dragon.
The brave knight set out to slay a dragon.
